+# Paper code: single portable evidence bundle
+
+The final **code.zip** contains code, actual frozen v6/v5 results, recovered
+historical plotting data/metadata, preserved plotting entry points, input PDFs,
+and per-file checksums. It is not necessary to combine three separate result
+ZIPs. The earlier three ZIPs are audit intermediates, not the final delivery.
+
+The original source ZIP contained 54 Python files and no raw results. This
+delivery adds newly reproduced controlled results and 537 existing historical
+data/metadata files (454,549,262 bytes) recovered from the related comparative-
+utility project, plus 16 relevant generator/helper sources. Eight original
+paper-figure PDFs and all twelve originally supplied empirical scripts matched
+that project byte-for-byte before the documented plotting compatibility fixes.
+Four real-LLM dashboard inputs also match its original saved SHA manifest.
+These assets do **not** replace the missing oral HANS/QA/ReCoRD protocol archives.
+
+See [the planner README](oral_planner_v6/README.md) for verified commands, output
+schemas, frozen settings, and results. Start module commands from this `code/`
+directory. The full planner reproduction uses CPU only.
+
+## Environment
+
+The verified full run used CPython 3.10.19, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.15.3, and
+Matplotlib 3.10.8 on Windows. If needed, install the observed versions with
+`python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` in an isolated Python 3.10 environment.
+The existing local `llm_reviewer` environment already has them. The source
+requires at least Python 3.9 (dictionary union and `Path.is_relative_to`); the
+pinned requirements target Python 3.10 or newer. Python 3.7 is insufficient.
+The archive does not record its original Python, NumPy, or BLAS versions, so
+these pins document the verified rerun rather than the historical environment.
+
+The original seven tests also pass with Python 3.9.25 / NumPy 2.0.2 / SciPy
+1.13.1. The complete frozen experiment was run only with the environment above.
+The optional HANS model runner additionally uses `requirements-model.txt`;
+installing packages does not restore missing data or authenticate model revisions.
+No new model training or inference was run during this audit. Optional training
+dependencies are observed local versions, not a validated training lock. For
+the packaged figure wrapper install `requirements-figures.txt`; model libraries
+are not needed. On machines without Times New Roman, the intro wrapper uses
+Matplotlib's DejaVu Serif, or accepts explicit TTF paths. No proprietary fonts
+are bundled; typography can differ with the font while PDF panels remain intact.
+Historical **vector-only** appendix PDF reflow additionally needs a local
+Chrome/Chromium-compatible browser, because its SVG clipping must be preserved
+by the original print backend. The wrapper discovers standard installed paths
+or accepts `--chrome PATH`; no browser is bundled or downloaded. Main/intro/cost
+plots and appendix data redraws do not need a browser. To omit vector-only
+reflow, use `--appendix-groups analytic,matched,cluster,hans,qwen_paired,p0,boundaries,dashboard`.
+
+## Use one ZIP, without machine-specific paths
+
+Unzip `code.zip` to obtain a `code/` directory. The controlled data and main/intro
+and planner-cost plotting workflows work from this directory alone. If using the matching LaTeX
+package for appendix redraws, unpack both into the same project root:
+
+```text
+project/
+  main.tex, appendix.tex, figures/, experiments/    # matching LaTeX package
+  code/                                          # this code.zip
+    oral_planner_v6/results/
+    oral_attribution_v5/results/
+    overleaf/experiments/                         # recovered historical inputs
+    tools/figure_sources/                        # unchanged plot script copies
+    figure_inputs/                               # PDF inputs and repair metadata
+    figure_outputs/                              # approved reference PDF/SVGs, not runtime caches
+    figure_archive/                              # retired four-panel F34 and pre-seed-CI HANS versions
+```
+
+Run from `project/code`. These commands do not train models and create NEW
+output directories; they refuse to overwrite an existing output directory:
+
+```powershell
+python -m unittest discover -s oral_planner_v6/tests -v
+python -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -v
+python tools/verify_historical.py --output-dir ../historical_check
+python tools/verify_hans_intervals.py --output-dir ../hans_interval_check
+python tools/export_planner.py --output-dir ../planner_csv
+python tools/export_attribution.py --output-dir ../matched_csv
+python tools/reproduce_figures.py --output-dir ../plots_main --which main,intro,costs
+python tools/reproduce_figures.py --output-dir ../plots_appendix --which appendix --appendix-tex ../appendix.tex
+```
+
+`tools/figure_sources/plot_main_evidence.py`, `layout_intro_pdf.py`, `plot_planner_costs.py` and
+`figure_repairs.py` are byte-identical captured copies of the parent task's
+scripts; do not run those raw snapshots from their nested directory. The wrapper
+sets up an isolated project-shaped output tree and redirects historical inputs
+to packaged data. It leaves root research scripts, original PDFs, manuscript,
+and frozen data unchanged. Main outputs appear in `plots_main/figures/` and
+cost outputs under `plots_main/experiments/oral_planner_v6/`, and appendix outputs

+`FIGURE_RUN.json` records actual inputs, font choices, outputs and hashes.
+The appendix command reads the supplied appendix to check eligible figures and
+all 64 matched threshold triples; a mismatching manuscript stops the redraw.
+Do not copy outputs over a manuscript until its separate visual review passes.
+
+`FIGURE_ASSETS.json` captures the graphic task's version and input hashes.
+Metadata marked "staged" or "needs visual inspection" remains so in the bundle;
+successful execution does not convert that status into camera-ready acceptance.
+When final reviewed/installed metadata are present, those records bind the
+approved reference PDFs/SVGs in `figure_outputs/` to their actual hashes. These
+are not newly claimed empirical arrays, and regenerated figures need their own
+visual acceptance when fonts/renderers differ. Contact sheets, QA raster caches
+and browser profiles are excluded from the delivered ZIP.
+
+The final paper's F34 retains only matched corruption, prospective negative
+gates, and transfer slack. Its current renderer is the packaged final
+`figure_repairs.py` snapshot through the wrapper's `dashboard` group. The older
+four-panel `plot_real_llm_evidence.py`, fixed-feature decision/MAE analysis and

+script/PDF/SVG are retained separately under `figure_archive/`; running an old renderer does not
+recreate the current paper figure or reintroduce the removed predictor claims.
+
+The final `r3-seed-ci` HANS figures use two-sided 95% t intervals across five
+training seeds (df=4; multiplier rounded to 2.776445). In F25(b,c), the three
+heuristics are first averaged within each seed; they are not 15 independent
+replicates. F26(b) subtracts factual within each seed before computing the
+interval. Displayed means and the saved CSV are unchanged. This is an explicitly
+authorized postprocessing correction, not a claim that the original pooled/normal
+intervals were correct. `figure_inputs/metadata/hans_seed_ci_validation.json`
+records all 39 old/new interval widths and the actual per-seed values; the
+independent verifier checks them directly against the original CSV. The legacy
+HANS plotting source and original PDFs remain preserved as historical evidence;
+the r2 repaired source and figures are also in `figure_archive/hans_r2_before_seed_ci/`;
+use the final wrapper for the corrected paper figures.
